# jano editor

> A modern terminal editor with plugin support. nano simplicity. VS Code power. Zero bloat.

jano is a terminal-based text editor built with TypeScript and compiled into a single binary with Bun. It combines the simplicity of nano with the power of VS Code — shortcuts you already know, plugins for any language, and blazing fast performance.

## Key Facts

- Single binary installation — no Node.js, no runtime, no dependencies
- Familiar shortcuts: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+S work out of the box
- Plugin system: syntax highlighting, formatting, validation — one `jano plugin install` away
- Multi-cursor editing (Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down)
- Handles 60,000+ lines without lag
- MIT licensed, fully open source
- Available for Linux (x64), macOS (arm64), and Windows (x64)

## Installation

Linux / macOS:
curl -fsSL https://janoeditor.dev/install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):
irm https://janoeditor.dev/install.ps1 | iex

## Links

- Website: https://janoeditor.dev
- GitHub: https://github.com/jano-editor/jano
- Plugin Store: https://janoeditor.dev/plugins
- Documentation: https://janoeditor.dev/docs

## Plugins

Plugins are single TypeScript files that export a LanguagePlugin object. Available plugins include YAML, JSON, Shell, and Markdown support. Anyone can publish plugins via the plugin store by linking a GitHub repository.

## Comparison

- vs nano: jano adds plugins, multi-cursor, syntax highlighting, and formatting
- vs vim: jano uses familiar shortcuts — no modes, no steep learning curve
- vs VS Code: jano runs in the terminal, starts in milliseconds, and weighs a single binary
